=== PLAN ===
# Plan — a populated queue, and a GUI worth looking at

One task per `## Txx — title` heading. Statuses: `todo` → `doing` → `claimed` → `verified`,
or `blocked(<reason>)`. Only the manager edits this file.

## T01 — Make the frontend build reproducible
- status: verified
- complexity: simple
- deps:
- done-when: `git ls-files --error-unmatch frontend/package-lock.json && grep -q 'npm ci' frontend/Dockerfile && cd frontend && npm ci --silent && npm run build && cd .. && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"`

Commit `frontend/package-lock.json`, pin the `"latest"` specifiers in `frontend/package.json:11-17`
to what the lockfile resolved, switch `frontend/Dockerfile:3-4` from `npm install` to `npm ci`, and
gitignore the tsc leftovers (`frontend/*.tsbuildinfo`, `frontend/vite.config.js`,
`frontend/vite.config.d.ts`). Closes backlog B6.
Probe note: config-only, no revertible impl file — falsify by hand (remove the lockfile, confirm
`npm ci` fails).

## T02 — Introduce Alembic
- status: blocked(0001 skips-and-stamps on table names only, so a column-drifted legacy DB is marked migrated and left broken — see B10)
- complexity: complex
- deps:
- done-when: `cd backend && rm -f /tmp/t02.db && DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////tmp/t02.db uv run alembic upgrade head && ! grep -q 'ALTER TABLE' app/main.py`

Add `alembic` as a runtime dependency, scaffold `backend/alembic/` with `env.py` reading
`DATABASE_URL` from settings, and autogenerate an initial migration matching today's models. Remove
the hand-written `ALTER TABLE` and the `create_all` from startup (`backend/app/main.py:46`) — but
existing databases already have these tables, so the migration must be safe to stamp rather than
re-run. Tests must not regress: `backend/tests/conftest.py` currently builds schema via
`Base.metadata.create_all`, so decide and document whether tests migrate or keep `create_all`.
Probe note: scaffolding-shaped; falsify by hand.

## T03 — Encrypt message content at rest
- status: todo
- complexity: complex
- deps: T02
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k excerpt_is_encrypted_at_rest`

`Source.excerpt` holds up to 2000 chars of real mail and Teams content in plaintext
(`backend/app/services/graph.py:50`). Encrypt with the existing AES-GCM helper
(`backend/app/services/crypto.py:34`) under its **own AAD** — never reuse `b"workboard-graph-v1"`,
which belongs to the token store. Decrypt on read so the API and the GUI evidence blockquotes keep
working. Test first: persist a signal with a distinctive marker, assert the marker is absent from
the raw bytes of the database file. Ship the data migration as an Alembic revision (T02), including
rows written before this change.

## T04 — Dispatch sync per source kind
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T03
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k per_source_dispatch`

`sync()` is hardwired to Graph and asserts the connected Graph user id
(`backend/app/services/sync.py:35-50`). Introduce a registry keyed by `SourceKind` so another kind
registers without editing `sync()`. Prove it with a test that registers a fake kind and syncs it end
to end. Keep the Graph identity assertion for the Graph kind only. No new connector here.

## T05 — Promote actionable signals into work items
- status: todo
- complexity: complex
- deps: T04
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k promotion`

The missing link: `persist_signals` writes only `Source` rows (`backend/app/services/graph.py:45`)
and nothing calls `create_work_item` (`backend/app/services/work_items.py:42`), so the queue is
empty after every sync. One named, unit-testable function holds the heuristic with its rules in a
docstring: promote signals addressed directly to the user, skip automated/newsletter senders and
bulk mail, carry the excerpt across as `WorkEvidence`. Synthetic fixtures must include a newsletter
that must NOT promote and a direct message that must. `source_external_id` is unique
(`backend/app/models.py:41`), so promoting twice must not raise or duplicate —
`test_promotion_is_idempotent` covers it.

## T06 — Backfill the Sources already stored
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T05
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k backfill`

Promote `Source` rows written before T05 once, so the queue populates without waiting for a sync.
Re-running must be safe — run the backfill twice in the test and assert a stable count. Document
where it runs (startup vs explicit endpoint); if startup, it must not slow boot on an empty DB.
Probe note: test-shaped; falsify by hand (stub the body, confirm the test reddens).

## T07 — Index and paginate the list endpoints
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T06
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k "pagination or indexes"`

`GET /api/work-items` and `/api/sources` return every row (`backend/app/api/routes.py:66`) and
`backend/app/models.py` has no `index=True` anywhere. Add indexes on the columns actually filtered
and sorted (status, source_kind, updated_at, and `Source.external_id` beyond its unique constraint
if the query plan needs it) via an Alembic revision. Return a consistent envelope —
items, total, limit, offset — with a sane default limit and a cap. This changes the shape
`frontend/src/api.ts:33` consumes; T13 adapts the GUI, so leave the frontend working or coordinate
via that task.

## T08 — Promote and dismiss from the API
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T07
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k "promote_endpoint or dismiss_endpoint"`

Endpoints to correct the heuristic by hand: promote a `Source` the rules missed, and dismiss a
`WorkItem` that should not have been promoted. Dismiss must not delete provenance — prefer a status
transition over a hard delete, and make a dismissed item stay dismissed across re-syncs and the
T06 backfill (otherwise the next run promotes it again). Both are cookie-writable, so they need the
CSRF path (`backend/app/security.py:106-109`).

## T09 — Measure the heuristic against real mail
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T05
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run python -m app.tools.heuristic_eval --sample "${MAGIC_TOWER_SAMPLE:-$HOME/.magic-tower/labeled-sample.json}"`

A command that replays a labeled sample through the heuristic and reports precision and recall.
The sample is the owner's real mail and **must never enter the repository** — read it from a
gitignored local path, default `~/.magic-tower/labeled-sample.json`, and **exit 0 with a clear
message when the file is absent** so CI and other machines pass. Ship a documented sample schema
plus a small synthetic example committed in its place, and document how the owner exports and
labels theirs. Report counts, precision, recall, and list the misclassified items so the rules can
be tuned.

## T10 — Frontend test infrastructure and shadcn foundation
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T01
- done-when: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run`

There are no frontend tests today. Add vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom, a `test` script,
and one real test of the existing app. In the same task add Tailwind and the shadcn CLI setup so
later tasks can copy components in. Pin every version — no `"latest"` — and keep `npm ci` green.

## T11 — Three-pane Mail layout with command palette
- status: todo
- complexity: complex
- deps: T10
- done-when: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run -t "layout"`

Rebuild the shell on shadcn's Mail example: resizable list + detail panes, and `cmdk` for a command
palette. Replace `frontend/src/styles.css` rather than layering Tailwind over it, and leave no dead
CSS. Keep the existing behaviour that works — session/token handling (`frontend/src/api.ts:14`),
the demo-data fallback on 401/503 (`main.tsx:6-10,17`), and the dispatch clipboard copy.

## T12 — Triage view with grouping
- status: todo
- complexity: complex
- deps: T11, T08
- done-when: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run -t "triage"`

The view the owner actually wanted: promoted items grouped for triage (by source kind and thread —
deterministic grouping, no LLM). Tests assert that items group correctly, that an empty queue says
so instead of rendering blank, and that the group counts match the data.

## T13 — Wire pagination, promote and dismiss into the GUI
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T12
- done-when: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run -t "pagination or actions"`

Consume T07's envelope (items/total/limit/offset) instead of assuming a bare array
(`frontend/src/api.ts:33`), with load-more or pager controls. Wire T08's promote and dismiss,
including the CSRF header the write path requires. Tests assert the request carries the right
offset and that a dismissed item leaves the list.

## T14 — Prove it end to end and on CI
- status: todo
- complexity: normal
- deps: T13, T09
- done-when: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k sync_populates_api && test "$(gh run list --branch "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" --limit 1 --json headSha,conclusion -q '.[0].headSha+":"+.[0].conclusion')" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD):success"`

One backend test running a fixture sync through the whole path, asserting `GET /api/work-items`
returns promoted items with evidence. Extend `.github/workflows/ci.yml` to run the frontend tests
too — today it runs only pytest and the Docker build. Then push so CI runs on this exact commit;
a stale earlier run does not count.

=== CONTRACT ===
# Contract — a populated queue, and a GUI worth looking at

Approved: 2026-09-18 · Sealed by `.companion/contract.sha256`.
Changing this file after approval requires `/companion:contract` again; `companion build` refuses otherwise.

## Result
After a Graph sync, the GUI shows real work items grouped for triage instead of an empty queue, and
the owner can promote or dismiss them by hand when the heuristic gets it wrong. The heuristic is
measured against a labeled sample of the owner's real mail, not only invented fixtures. Mail and
chat content stops sitting in plaintext on disk. Schema changes go through Alembic instead of a
hand-written `ALTER TABLE`. Lists are indexed and paginated. `sync()` stops being hardwired to
Graph, so Jira and Freshservice can be added later without surgery.

## Non-goals
- Any Jira or Freshservice connector. This contract only makes room for them
  (`backend/app/services/sync.py:35-50` currently asserts the Graph-connected user id).
- Any LLM call. Promotion is deterministic rules; LLM cleaning and grouping is a later contract.
- MCP server / real agent hand-off. Dispatch stays a queue row and the clipboard copy of
  `pending-work context <id>`.
- Any LLM-based cleaning, titling or grouping. Grouping in this contract is deterministic
  (by source thread/kind), not semantic.
- Session persistence across API restart (`backend/app/security.py:31` stays a process-local dict)
  and authentication on `GET /api/sync/status` (`backend/app/api/sync.py:14`). Both are backlog.

## Environment facts
- test: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests ../tests/agent_protocol -q`
  — **runs today: 26 passed in 1.79s.**
- run: `docker compose build && docker compose up` (GUI same-origin behind nginx, which proxies
  `/api/` → `api:8000`, `frontend/nginx.conf:11`). Backend alone:
  `cd backend && DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./workboard.db uv run uvicorn app.main:app`.
- lint: none — no ruff/black/flake8/mypy configured.
- dead-code: `{ ( cd backend && uv run --with vulture vulture app tests --min-confidence 80 | wc -l ); ( cd frontend && npx --yes knip@latest --reporter json 2>/dev/null | jq '[.issues[] | (.files|length)+(.exports|length)+(.types|length)+(.dependencies|length)+(.devDependencies|length)+(.unlisted|length)+(.unresolved|length)+(.duplicates|length)+(.enumMembers|length)+(.namespaceMembers|length)+(.binaries|length)] | add // 0' ); } | paste -sd+ | bc`
  — **baseline 4 today**, covering *both* languages. Python side (vulture, 2): both `cls` in
  `@classmethod` pydantic validators (`backend/app/config.py:34,45`), false positives; do not use
  vulture's default 60% confidence, which reports 80 findings that are nearly all pydantic fields
  and SQLAlchemy columns. TypeScript side (knip, 2): the generated `frontend/vite.config.d.ts`
  (removed by T01) and an unused exported type `Evidence` (`frontend/src/api.ts:5`). knip runs
  zero-config here and counts unused files, exports, types, dependencies and unresolved imports, so
  the shadcn rebuild cannot hide dead TS or CSS behind a Python-only gate.
- Python 3.12 + uv; Node 22 for the frontend (`frontend/Dockerfile:1`).
- **There are no frontend tests today** — `frontend/src/` is 4 files and `frontend/package.json`
  has no vitest/jest/testing-library/playwright dependency. Test infrastructure is part of T10, and
  no GUI acceptance criterion can be written before it exists.
- **There is no Alembic today** — startup does `create_all` plus a hand-written `ALTER TABLE`
  (`backend/app/main.py:46`), and `alembic` is not a dependency.
- The labeled real-mail sample is **local and gitignored**; CI and every committed test run on
  synthetic fixtures only. No real mail content ever enters the repository.
- **The test command must be run from `backend/`** — `env_file=".env"` is cwd-relative
  (`backend/app/config.py:13`), so from the repo root the root `.env`'s empty `MICROSOFT_*` values
  abort collection with 3 pydantic ValidationErrors.
- `httpx` is currently a **dev-only** dependency; `EncryptedTokenStore` is single-slot, one path and
  AAD `b"workboard-graph-v1"` (`backend/app/services/crypto.py:23-48`).
- Untracked in the tree at sealing: `frontend/package-lock.json` (keep, T01),
  `frontend/tsconfig*.tsbuildinfo`, `frontend/vite.config.js`, `frontend/vite.config.d.ts`
  (generated by tsc despite `noEmit`; gitignore them).

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: The whole backend suite is green, including every new test this contract adds.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests ../tests/agent_protocol -q`
- AC2: The frontend builds from a committed lockfile, and the image uses `npm ci`.
  - verify: `git ls-files --error-unmatch frontend/package-lock.json && grep -q 'npm ci' frontend/Dockerfile && cd frontend && npm ci --silent && npm run build`
- AC3: A full build leaves the tree clean — no generated artefact is untracked or unignored.
  - verify: `cd frontend && npm run build >/dev/null 2>&1; cd .. && test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"`
- AC4: Schema changes go through Alembic; the migration chain applies to an empty database and
  startup no longer hand-writes DDL.
  - verify: `cd backend && rm -f /tmp/ac4-alembic.db && DATABASE_URL=sqlite:////tmp/ac4-alembic.db uv run alembic upgrade head && ! grep -q 'ALTER TABLE' app/main.py`
- AC5: Message content is not readable in the database file.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k excerpt_is_encrypted_at_rest`
- AC6: `sync()` dispatches per source kind; a second kind registers without editing `sync()`.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k per_source_dispatch`
- AC7: A sync promotes actionable signals into work items, ignores noise, and does not duplicate
  on a second run.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k promotion`
- AC8: Sources stored before this change are promoted once, by a backfill that is safe to re-run.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k backfill`
- AC9: List endpoints are paginated and the columns they filter and sort on are indexed.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k "pagination or indexes"`
- AC10: The owner can promote a missed Source and dismiss a wrongly-promoted item through the API.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run pytest tests -q -k "promote_endpoint or dismiss_endpoint"`
- AC11: The heuristic is measured against the owner's labeled real-mail sample, and the command
  reports precision and recall. It skips cleanly when the gitignored sample is absent.
  - verify: `cd backend && uv run python -m app.tools.heuristic_eval --sample "${MAGIC_TOWER_SAMPLE:-$HOME/.magic-tower/labeled-sample.json}"`
- AC12: The frontend has tests and they pass.
  - verify: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run`
- AC13: The GUI renders grouped triage items, paginates, and can promote/dismiss — proven by

content.content:
## Quality bar
- Tests first; every behaviour change has a test that fails without it. For the heuristic in
  particular, the fixtures must include both a newsletter/automated sender that must NOT be
  promoted and a direct message that must be.
- The heuristic lives in one named, unit-testable function with its rules stated in a docstring —
  not scattered through `persist_signals`.
- No dead code (baseline 2, false positives only), no debug output, no unrelated formatting churn.
- Matches existing conventions: sync `def` routes, module-level `app`, injectable transports for
  I/O (`backend/app/integrations/graph.py:18-36`), `"kind:{external_id}"` prefixes for
  `Source.external_id`.
- Paginated list endpoints return a consistent envelope — items, total, limit, offset — and the
  frontend consumes it rather than assuming a bare array (`frontend/src/api.ts:33`).
- **No real mail content in the repository.** The labeled sample stays at a gitignored local path;
  committed fixtures are synthetic.
- The shadcn rebuild replaces `frontend/src/styles.css` rather than layering Tailwind on top of it;
  no dead CSS left behind.
- Secrets stay out of source. Encryption uses the existing AES-GCM helper with its own AAD, never a
  second hardcoded key. Nothing weakens the fail-closed 503, the CSRF check, or
  `hmac.compare_digest`.

## Playbook checks applied
---AC12/13---
83:- AC12: The frontend has tests and they pass.
84-  - verify: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run`
85:- AC13: The GUI renders grouped triage items, paginates, and can promote/dismiss — proven by
86-  frontend tests, not by the build succeeding.
87-  - verify: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run -t "triage"`
---RESULT---
## Result
After a Graph sync, the GUI shows real work items grouped for triage instead of an empty queue, and
the owner can promote or dismiss them by hand when the heuristic gets it wrong. The heuristic is
measured against a labeled sample of the owner's real mail, not only invented fixtures. Mail and
chat content stops sitting in plaintext on disk. Schema changes go through Alembic instead of a
hand-written `ALTER TABLE`. Lists are indexed and paginated. `sync()` stops being hardwired to
Graph, so Jira and Freshservice can be added later without surgery.

## Non-goals

Get it with: git -C /home/eimi/projects/magic-tower diff 6904b2c4657e2680e83ae84ec309b48d551cf9dd..HEAD (`frontend/package-lock.json` is ~1800 lines of that diff; use `-- . ':!frontend/package-lock.json'` to read the substantive part, and inspect the lockfile separately if you need to.) # The task (verbatim from .companion/plan.md) ## T10 — Frontend test infrastructure and shadcn foundation - status: doing - complexity: normal - deps: T01 - done-when: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run` There are no frontend tests today. Add vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom, a `test` script, and one real test of the existing app. In the same task add Tailwind and the shadcn CLI setup so later tasks can copy components in. Pin every version — no `"latest"` — and keep `npm ci` green. # Contract excerpt Acceptance criterion this task serves: - AC12: The frontend has tests and they pass. verify: `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run` Quality bar (verbatim, the clauses that bear on this task): - Tests first; every behaviour change has a test that fails without it. - No dead code (baseline 4 at sealing, 3 today), no debug output, no unrelated formatting churn. The dead-code command covers both languages (vulture + knip). - The shadcn rebuild replaces `frontend/src/styles.css` rather than layering Tailwind on top of it; no dead CSS left behind. - Secrets stay out of source. - Matches existing conventions. Relevant downstream tasks (context for how much drift is tolerable): - T11 (complexity complex, deps T10): "Rebuild the shell on shadcn's Mail example: resizable list + detail panes, and `cmdk` for a command palette. Replace `frontend/src/styles.css` rather than layering Tailwind over it, and leave no dead CSS." So T11 is the task that owns replacing styles.css. - T12/T13 consume shadcn components and the paginated envelope. # Worker report (model output — claims, not facts; verify anything that matters) The worker (sonnet) reports: added vitest ^5.0.1, jsdom ^30.1.0, @testing-library/react ^16.3.3, @testing-library/dom ^10.4.2, tailwindcss ^4.3.3, @tailwindcss/vite ^4.3.3 as devDependencies and a `test: vitest` script; switched `vite.config.ts` to `defineConfig` from `vitest/config` with the tailwind plugin, an `@` → `./src` alias and `test: { environment: 'jsdom' }`; added `paths` to tsconfig.json; added `"DOM"` to `lib` in tsconfig.node.json; extracted `App` out of `main.tsx` into a new `frontend/src/App.tsx` (claimed verbatim) leaving main.tsx as the React bootstrap; added `frontend/src/App.test.tsx`; prepended `@import "tailwindcss";` to `src/styles.css`; added `frontend/components.json` for the shadcn CLI. Two worker claims you should scrutinise specifically: 1. It claims `App.tsx` is the old `main.tsx` App/Detail/Settings/demoItems/labels "extracted verbatim". Verify that — a silent behaviour change smuggled into an "extraction" is the thing most worth catching here. 2. It claims "styles.css is the single live stylesheet... Appearance is preserved", justified by grepping that original rules like `.topbar{border-bottom:1px solid #4b3854;...}` survive in the built CSS. See my finding below; I believe that justification does not support the claim. It deliberately did NOT add `frontend/src/lib/utils.ts` (shadcn's `cn` helper), reasoning that an unimported file would raise the knip dead-code count, and that `npx shadcn add` creates it on first use in T11. Judge whether that leaves the shadcn foundation actually usable by T11 or merely nominally configured. # Probe result Vacuity probe: **RED**, but weakly so — reverting the 9 implementation files removes the `test` script itself, so npm failed with `Missing script: "test"`. That RED proves only that no test script existed at base. It proves nothing about whether the test depends on the app. I therefore hand-falsified (below). # What I verified myself (manager), with results - `git log 6904b2c..branch` → one commit, bfcc54d. Fast-forward merged cleanly. - done-when `cd frontend && npm run test -- --run` in main tree after `npm ci` → **exit 0**, 1 passed. - Contract test `cd backend && uv run pytest tests ../tests/agent_protocol -q` → **exit 0**, 31 passed (26 in the contract is pre-T02 drift, not caused here). - `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) → **exit 0**. - Dead-code gate (vulture + knip) → **3**, unchanged from today's baseline of 3. - **Fresh clone** of bfcc54d to /tmp, `npm ci` → exit 0, done-when → exit 0, build → exit 0, identical bundle hash `index-sZYBVqeB.js`. (This project has been burned once by a warm cache making a broken commit look green, so I check fresh clones now.) - `git status --porcelain` clean apart from my own `.companion/plan.md` edit and the known untracked `.claude/` agent-worktree dir. - **Hand falsification of the test** (since the probe was weak): I gutted the offline-fallback branch in `App.tsx` — changed `catch { ... setState('offline'); setDemo(true); setItems(demoItems); setSelected(demoItems[0]) }` to just `setState('offline')` — and the test went **RED** (exit 1, `TestingLibraryElementError`, findAllByText found no match). Restored → green. So the test does exercise the real fallback code path, not merely a string literal. # My open finding for you to weigh (I did not treat it as blocking on my own) The worker's "appearance is preserved" claim is not supported. Tailwind v4.3.3 preflight **is** injected into the built CSS. Concretely, from `frontend/dist/assets/index-BAvVTd-x.css` (11,594 bytes built vs 7,427 bytes of source `styles.css`): - The build emits `@layer theme{...}`, `@layer base{...}`, `@layer utilities{...}`, with app CSS unlayered after them. - `@layer base` contains `h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6{font-size:inherit;font-weight:inherit}`. - Unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity, so the app's own rules win **for properties they actually declare**. The app declares `font-size` for its headings (`.brand h1`, `h2`, `.detail h3`, `.modal h3`, `.detail h4`) but declares `font-weight` **only on h4**. - Consequence as I read it: `

Magic Tower

`, the `

Gather every signal…

` hero, and `

{item.title}

` lose their browser-default bold and render at normal weight. Preflight also resets list-style and element margins. Please check my reading of the cascade — I may be wrong about which side wins. Then judge whether this is blocking for T10 given that T11 replaces `styles.css` wholesale, or whether it is an advisory the next task absorbs. Say which, explicitly. # Also please judge - Is the single test meaningful enough to satisfy "one real test of the existing app", or is it thin to the point of being decorative? - Is `"DOM"` added to `tsconfig.node.json`'s `lib` a legitimate need or a workaround masking a misconfiguration? - Are all versions genuinely pinned per T01's convention (caret ranges matching the lockfile are fine; a bare `"latest"` is not), and is the lockfile in sync? - Is vitest ^5.0.1 / tailwindcss ^4.3.3 / @testing-library/react ^16.3.3 a coherent set against vite 8 + typescript 7 + react 19, or is there a version trap that will surface in T11? - Any secrets, debug output, or unrelated formatting churn. - Does extracting App into its own file break anything T11/T12/T13 rely on, or help them? Return your verdict as `approve` or `revise`. If `revise`, give falsifiable blocking findings — each one something I can check by running a command or reading a specific line — and put the single most important one first. Advisories that should not block go in a clearly separate list.

content.text:
Review delivered: **revise**, with two blocking findings.

The headline is that the worker's "appearance is preserved" claim is false, and the manager's own reading of the cascade was correct but too narrow — no heading in the app declares `font-weight` at all, so Tailwind preflight de-bolds every one of them, and the unlock form's password input additionally loses its border, padding, and background. The second blocking finding is new: Tailwind v4's source scanner makes `docker compose build web` emit a different CSS artifact (11.59 kB vs 14.43 kB) depending on whether a stale `dist/` sits in the build context, because there is no `.dockerignore` and the root `.gitignore` never reaches the image.

Everything else checked out — the App extraction is byte-identical, versions are genuinely pinned and peer-coherent, the `DOM` lib addition is a real need, the `@` alias resolves under both `tsc` and `vitest`, and skipping `lib/utils.ts` was the right call. I also confirmed the worker was boxed into touching `styles.css`: removing the import pushes the knip gate from 3 to 4.

Repair dispatched (attempt 2, opus, fresh worker — never reusing a failed one). Where things stand:

**Attempt 1 rejected.** Both blocking findings held up when I reproduced them myself, and one of them corrected me:

- **Preflight de-bolds the whole GUI.** I had told the reviewer the app declares `font-weight` on `h4`; it doesn't. My regex had matched `h4 small` — a different selector. Source `styles.css` declares `font-weight` on *no* heading, so every heading drops to 400, not just h1–h3. The reviewer also caught something I'd missed entirely: preflight strips `.sync form input` — the LOCAL_API_TOKEN unlock field — of its border, padding and background, leaving near-white text on a dark panel.
- **The build stopped being reproducible**, measured above: 14,437 bytes with a stale `dist/` in context vs 11,594 from a clean one, same commit and lockfile.

I'd been inclined to let the CSS issue through as an advisory, reasoning T11 replaces `styles.css` anyway. The reviewer rejected that and I think it's right: T11 is gated on T10 and may not land, so the degraded UI would be what's on `main` in the meantime. I deferred to it rather than overriding.

Notably, the worker was somewhat boxed in — dropping the Tailwind import entirely makes knip flag `tailwindcss` as an unused devDependency, pushing the dead-code gate 3 → 4. The fix is a narrower import (`tailwindcss/theme.css` + `tailwindcss/utilities.css`), not removing Tailwind.

Attempt 1 is preserved as tag `t10-attempt1-rejected`, `main` is reset to `6904b2c`, and the findings are in `progress.md`. The repair prompt tells the new worker to reuse the verified parts — the App extraction, pinning, tsconfig `"DOM"` fix, and components.json all checked out — and demands a falsifiable before/after for each finding. Per the ladder, if this attempt fails review, T10 is blocked rather than repaired again.

    build:
      context: ./backend
    env_file:
      - path: .env
        required: false

      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-sqlite:////data/workboard.db}

      - workboard-data:/data
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    expose:
      - "8000"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/api/health')"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  web:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
    depends_on:
      api:

    ports:

    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /var/cache/nginx
      - /var/run
      - /tmp
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true

      - ALL
    cap_add:
      - CHOWN
      - SETUID
      - SETGID

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat: add frontend test infrastructure and shadcn/Tailwind foundation

Adds vitest + @testing-library/react + jsdom with a `test` script and a
real test of the offline-fallback path, plus Tailwind v4 and the shadcn
CLI config so later tasks can copy components in. Every version pinned.

Tailwind is imported as `tailwindcss/theme.css` + `tailwindcss/utilities.css`
rather than the `tailwindcss` umbrella, so preflight never reaches the
bundle: the umbrella import injects `h1..h6{font-weight:inherit}` and a
universal `border:0;padding:0;background-color:#0000` reset into
`@layer base`, which unlayered app CSS cannot outrank, unbolding every
heading and stripping the LOCAL_API_TOKEN unlock field. The split import
keeps every utility, variant and theme token available for shadcn.

`frontend/.dockerignore` keeps build artefacts out of the build context.
Tailwind v4 source detection scans the whole context and cannot see the
root .gitignore, so a stale local `dist/` was being scanned as source and
changed the emitted CSS (10.31 kB vs 7.45 kB at the same commit).

To keep `main.tsx` testable, `App` moves to `App.tsx` unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Answers to your five open questions.

**1. Is the entrypoint split legitimate? Yes — not a trick.** `tailwindcss@4.3.3`'s own `package.json` `exports` map explicitly publishes `"./theme.css"`, `"./theme"`, `"./utilities.css"`, `"./utilities"`, `"./preflight.css"`, `"./preflight"`. These are public API; a patch release removing them would be a semver break. I confirmed utilities and variants genuinely compile under the split — `.md\:flex{display:flex}` inside `@media (width>=48rem)`, `.hover\:bg-neutral-700:hover{background-color:var(--color-neutral-700)}`, `focus-visible:ring-2` with full `--tw-ring-shadow` chain, `dark:bg-neutral-800`, and `--color-neutral-500` theme tokens. Nothing is degraded by the split.

**2. Unlayered utilities — does it trap T11? The worker's reading is right, and the choice is *better* than the umbrella, not worse.** I confirmed `theme.css` is a bare `@theme default{...}` and `utilities.css` is literally one line, `@tailwind utilities;` — no `layer()` wrapper, while `index.css` opens with `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;`. The key cascade fact: **layered CSS always loses to unlayered CSS regardless of specificity.** So with the umbrella, `.flex` (in `@layer utilities`) would lose to *every* unlayered app rule, including bare `button{cursor:pointer}`. Unlayered utilities at least fight on specificity. The residual trap is advisory 3 above and is one `@layer legacy{}` wrapper away from fixed. T10 improved T11's position here.

**3. Was dropping preflight the right call? Yes — and the specific dependency you feared is not real in v4.** This is the one you flagged as most costly to get wrong, so I tested it rather than reasoned it. Tailwind v4's border utility is **self-sufficient**: it emits `.border{border-style:var(--tw-border-style);border-width:1px}` together with `@property --tw-border-style{syntax:"*";inherits:false;initial-value:solid}` and a `@layer properties` fallback block. That was the v3 behaviour that needed preflight's `border:0 solid`; v4 no longer does. `box-sizing` is already covered by the app's own `*{box-sizing:border-box}`. So shadcn's `border`/`border-input` work fine without preflight, and the residual gap is narrow and enumerated in advisory 2. Keeping preflight would have re-introduced the attempt-1 blocker (every heading at weight 400) — there was no version of "keep it" that passed. Importantly, T11 is **not** trapped: re-adding preflight `layer(base)` later is additive and non-breaking, because layered preflight loses to the unlayered app CSS.

**4. `.dockerignore` — all five entries correct, none excludes a build input.** Context is `frontend/`; the Dockerfile copies `package*.json`, runs `npm ci`, copies `.`, runs `tsc -b && vite build`. `node_modules`/`dist` are regenerated. ---
name: probe-red-is-vacuous-when-impl-owns-the-test-runner
description: A vacuity probe that reverts impl files proves nothing when those files also install the test runner — RED just means "no test script".
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When a task's implementation includes the test harness itself (adding vitest, a `test` script,
a conftest, a new runner config), the vacuity probe reverts that harness along with the code and
reports RED for the wrong reason — on magic-tower T10 it reverted 9 files and failed with
`npm error Missing script: "test"`. That RED only proves no test existed at base; it says nothing
about whether the test exercises the implementation.

This is distinct from the known "test-only and docs-only tasks need hand falsification" rule in
`.companion/playbook.md`. Here the task *does* have revertible impl files, so the probe looks
applicable and returns a confident-looking RED. It is vacuous by construction.

**Why:** the probe's premise is that reverting impl while keeping tests should redden the tests.
That premise breaks when impl and harness are the same change set.

**How to apply:** before trusting a probe's RED, read *why* it failed, not just the verdict. If the
failure is "runner/script/config missing" rather than an assertion failing, hand-falsify instead:
mutate one behaviour the test claims to cover and confirm it reddens on an assertion. On T10 this
caught a real defect the probe and the worker both missed — the assertion
`expect(...).not.toHaveLength(0)` was a tautology (the query rejects before the matcher runs), and
a mutation that emptied the detail pane passed it while `toHaveLength(2)` failed it.

Expect this to recur on every frontend task in this repo (T11–T13 all run `npm run test`).

Related: [[falsify-each-clause-of-a-compound-gate]], [[verify-artifacts-through-their-consumer]].

**T10 verified** on attempt 2 (`ab5ec9b`), recorded in `.companion/progress.md`, plan status updated, committed as `60591d3`. Session ends here.

**What happened:** attempt 1 (sonnet) passed every mechanical gate — done-when, tests, build, dead-code, fresh clone — and was still wrong. Review caught two blocking defects, both of which I reproduced by hand before acting:

- Tailwind's preflight umbrella de-bolded every heading in the GUI and stripped the LOCAL_API_TOKEN unlock field of its border, padding and background. The worker's report asserted "appearance is preserved."
- The build stopped being reproducible: the same commit emitted 14,437 vs 11,594 bytes of CSS depending on whether a stale `dist/` sat in the Docker context — undoing the point of T01.

The repair (opus) fixed both in a three-file delta, reusing attempt 1's verified work byte-for-byte. I confirmed each fix by the falsifiable test rather than the diff: no preflight survives in the built CSS while every app rule does, and two image builds from deliberately different contexts now produce an identical artifact.

**Two things worth your attention:**

I was wrong on a detail and it mattered. I told the first reviewer the app declared `font-weight` on `h4`; it declares it on no heading at all — my regex had matched a `h4 small` selector. The reviewer caught it and found a second regression I'd missed entirely. I'd also been inclined to wave the CSS issue through as an advisory since T11 replaces `styles.css`; the reviewer rejected that on the grounds that T11 is gated on T10 and may never land, which I think is right, so I deferred rather than overrode.

The vacuity probe is structurally broken for this task family. Reverting the implementation deletes the `test` script itself, so it fails with `Missing script: "test"` — a confident-looking RED that proves only that no test existed at base. Both attempts needed hand falsification instead, and that's what exposed attempt 1's assertion as a tautology: `not.toHaveLength(0)` can never fail, because the query rejects before the matcher runs. A mutation that left the list populated but the detail pane empty passed the old assertion and fails the new one. Expect this on T11–T13 too; I've saved it to memory.

Three advisories are filed as B13–B15 for T11, one of which is a trap worth knowing about in advance: `components.json` sets `cssVariables: true` with no token block, so the first shadcn button T11 copies in will render invisible until `shadcn init` is run. B9 is now closed.

T11 is unblocked (dep T10 verified). T02 remains blocked, so T03–T09 stay gated behind it.

**What happened:** attempt 1 (sonnet) passed every mechanical gate — done-when, tests, build, dead-code, fresh clone — and was still wrong. Review caught two blocking defects, both of which I reproduced by hand before acting:

- Tailwind's preflight umbrella de-bolded every heading in the GUI and stripped the LOCAL_API_TOKEN unlock field of its border, padding and background. The worker's report asserted "appearance is preserved."
- The build stopped being reproducible: the same commit emitted 14,437 vs 11,594 bytes of CSS depending on whether a stale `dist/` sat in the Docker context — undoing the point of T01.

The repair (opus) fixed both in a three-file delta, reusing attempt 1's verified work byte-for-byte. I confirmed each fix by the falsifiable test rather than the diff: no preflight survives in the built CSS while every app rule does, and two image builds from deliberately different contexts now produce an identical artifact.

**Two things worth your attention:**

I was wrong on a detail and it mattered. I told the first reviewer the app declared `font-weight` on `h4`; it declares it on no heading at all — my regex had matched a `h4 small` selector. The reviewer caught it and found a second regression I'd missed entirely. I'd also been inclined to wave the CSS issue through as an advisory since T11 replaces `styles.css`; the reviewer rejected that on the grounds that T11 is gated on T10 and may never land, which I think is right, so I deferred rather than overrode.

The vacuity probe is structurally broken for this task family. Reverting the implementation deletes the `test` script itself, so it fails with `Missing script: "test"` — a confident-looking RED that proves only that no test existed at base. Both attempts needed hand falsification instead, and that's what exposed attempt 1's assertion as a tautology: `not.toHaveLength(0)` can never fail, because the query rejects before the matcher runs. A mutation that left the list populated but the detail pane empty passed the old assertion and fails the new one. Expect this on T11–T13 too; I've saved it to memory.

Three advisories are filed as B13–B15 for T11, one of which is a trap worth knowing about in advance: `components.json` sets `cssVariables: true` with no token block, so the first shadcn button T11 copies in will render invisible until `shadcn init` is run. B9 is now closed.

T11 is unblocked (dep T10 verified). T02 remains blocked, so T03–T09 stay gated behind it.
